title: Asset creation with AI:s
author: mcknschn
selftext:
I'm creating a quiz-game for my nephew, it's a simple game where you answer questions with given time limit stressing the player. There isn't much of a story in the game but I'm trying to create som kind of backstory and characters but I'm having a hard time with the asset creation with AI - it's just not as visually compelling as I'd like it to be. I'm using React + three.js for the frontend. 

Any tips on asset creation with AI? I'm seeing a lot of very nice looking games being created, what are you guys using?

comments.author: saumanahaii
comments.body: What are you using?  Straight Codex/ Claude or a dedicated service like Tripo?  2d or 3d?

replies.author: mcknschn
replies.body: First I just used Claude and just described the visuals with text and reached an OK level I'd said. But then I wanted to create nicer looking visuals so I had ChatGPT create some reference images which looked quite nice but Claude has been really bad at implementing them into the game. It's 3D or maybe 2.5D, the characters are mostly still and are doing some small movements

comments.author: Hidden-Method
comments.body: Great thought, it’s heaps of fun to have kids as creative directors :D If it’s just a quiz game and you don’t need multiple frame animations codex/geppetto is your best buddy. It‘s a bit of work and experience to not get the obvious openai look, but you‘ll have a lot of fun experimenting. Good luck and hopefully lots of fun times with your nephew!

comments.author: Jolva
comments.body: You could, for example, have ChatGPT or Gemini create an image reference for a character you like with no background. Then you could feed that image into a system like Tripio or Meshy. Those systems would be able to export that as a 3D mesh with textures (.glb) that you could import into your game. If you really wanna go nuts switch to Unity with an MCP connection.

replies.author: mcknschn
replies.body: Thanks! Will try it out. I kind of thought Unity was only for desktop games but can they do browser games as well? My thinking is that the game needs to be lite because it will probably be played on quite cheap computers

comments.body:

看看有沒有我能幫忙的

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: Give your agent blender skills and have it try to create the assets in blender

replies.author: jeaksaw
replies.body: Is there any skills that you have tried for Blender? Can you share some results?
